newsitem.title: USA: Tribune Q1 education loss vs profit.
newsitem.headline: Tribune Q1 education loss vs profit.

text.p: Tribune Co, a broadcast and publishing company, said its education division reported an operating loss of $200,000 in the first quarter, compared with a year-ago profit of $2.2 million.

The loss was due primarily to acquisitions of Educational Publishing Corp and NTC Publishing Group in March 1996, Tribune said. First quarter results for these companies reflect the seasonality of their businesses, it added.
First quarter education revenues rose 66 percent to $37 million from $23 million, due to acquisitions and improvements in existing business units. Excluding acquisitions, revenues were up 12 percent.
Tribune's education division publishes supplemental education and core curriculum materials.
Earlier, Tribune reported earnings from continuing operations of $0.49 a primary share, up from $0.37 a year ago.
Tribune said its interest expense in the quater rose 42 percent to $16 million from $11 million a year ago due to higher debt levels for acquisitions and stock repurchases.
